Slender arched bridges of pale carved stone span between the towers, their railings worked into flowing leaf-and-vine patterns.
Glowing fairy-lanterns like captured starlight hang strung between the spires, casting soft silver light across the walkways.
Living trees have been grown into the white architecture itself, their luminous boughs forming natural arches over the bridges.
Delicate spiral staircases of white stone wind up the tower interiors, each step edged with faintly glowing carved fern-fronds.
Gossamer banners drift from the high balconies, their pale silk woven through with fae-thread that shimmers without any wind.
Glowing vines climb the outer tower walls, their soft green light pulsing gently like slow and steady breathing.
Warm amber light spills from tall narrow windows, casting gold pools across the pale stone courtyards far below.
Still reflecting pools mirror the spires above, their surfaces threaded with slow-drifting motes of fae light from beneath.
Graceful fountains pour silver water in arcing threads between tiered basins carved with the faces of ancient elf-lords.
Tall graceful statues of elf-lords line the grand promenades, their stone faces serene, their outstretched hands holding living blossoms.
Flowering creepers cascade down every wall and balcony, their pale blooms exhaling a faint luminescence in the evening air.
Thin white spires taper to needle-fine points, each tip capped with a soft hovering sphere of warm fae-light.
Glowing crystal lamps are set into the archway keystones, their cold blue light refracting into prismatic fans across the stone.
Woven-branch archways frame the city gates, their intertwined boughs draped in drifting golden motes of slow-spinning fae magic.
The white stonework is carved entirely into cascading leaf forms, each surface flowing into the next like frozen water.
Narrow balconies project from the towers on curved stone brackets shaped like unfurling fern fronds caught mid-spiral.
Pale moths the size of palms drift lazily between the lanterns, their wings dusted in fae-light that never fades.
The cobblestones are inlaid with delicate silver tracery that glows faintly underfoot, mapping the old star-paths of the city.
Hanging gardens of silver-leafed plants spill from the upper terraces, their trailing roots woven through with soft threads of light.
Slender bell-towers chime without bells, their resonant tones conjured by fae wind-magic channeled through carved hollow spire-columns.
Fine filigree gates of wrought white metal stand at each courtyard entrance, their scrollwork alive with tiny carved woodland creatures.
Moss of impossible green carpets every shaded step and ledge, faintly phosphorescent where fae-light has seeped deep into the roots.
The great hall ceiling is a living canopy of interwoven boughs, small glowing buds opening and closing like slow breath.
Mist pools softly at the base of each tower each morning, thinning only where fae-ward stones keep the pathways clear.
Carved elf-lord faces emerge from the tower facades at every floor, their stone eyes inset with chips of glowing amber crystal.
